chapter_theme: Songs at Thiruthavathurai (திருத்தவத்துறை, Lalgudi) on the Kaveri: two courtesan songs whose pleas ask to leave the women's delusion and to be raised among the devotees, with praise of the vel that taught Siva and of the shrine's goddess who fosters dharma.

918.reading: The poet describes courtesans who gather and tie up their dark hair for others to see, roll eyes that reach their ears, grow deceit in their minds, make the wealth in lustful men's hands their kin, bare breasts like full pots and put a price on anyone's heart, and asks for grace to leave their delusion. The praise shows ghouls dancing to drums and vultures circling, Siva on the bull dancing like a spun top, and names Murugan the hero of Thiruthavathurai on the Kaveri, who crushed the demons and cut the gods free.
918.nuance: காமுகர் அன்பு புகுவித்த கைப்பொருள் உறவாகி: the women's kinship is with the money, not the man, and யாரையும் நெஞ்சை விலைப்படுத்திடு, pricing anyone's heart, says the trade reaches the heart itself.

919.reading: The poet speaks of women in pearl garlands with bent waists and fine garments who fill men of wealth with infatuation and stand daily in the streets with cuckoo voices, and asks whether, so that he does not whirl in their net but lives praising the anklets, Murugan will not speak the word that raises him, a sinner of low quality, to the high state in the assembly of devotees. The praise names the vel that spoke true jnana into the ear of Siva who dwells in the hearts of great ascetics, mansions where the fame of the Thiruvasagam spreads, the Kaveri's floods and heaped paddy, Seyppathi, and the goddess of eternal auspiciousness who fosters dharma, at Thiruthavathurai.
919.nuance: அத்தமுளோர் தமையே மயல் நிரப்பி: the women choose men of wealth. The plea is for a place in the சபை of devotees, a social salvation. The line on the Thiruvasagam spoken by the great one among Tamil scholars seems to refer to Manikkavasagar's work, but its syntax is unclear to me. அறம் வளர்த்த நித்ய கல்யாணி names the goddess as the one who fosters dharma.
